concepts.definition: The frames-and-context family F1 concerns bounded engagement: frame declaration, sizing, binding, activation, relations, coverage and revision. The reference-frame-evaluation member owns engagement under urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation; ACTIVATION owns context construction and FOUNDATIONS owns the referenced frame objects, authority kinds, independence distinctions and frame tuple.

grounding.quote:
decides how a finite actor engages a body of work through bounded reference
frames: how a frame is declared, sized, bound, activated, related to other
frames, used to audit coverage and revised.

concepts.label: Frames and context

conditions: Instance premises describe the governed work rather than commitments derivable from finite capacity alone.
concepts.definition: The foundation-to-law table traces consequences, stating rules, added choices, owners, pillars and consumers; it owns none of the named rules. Its instance premises are workspace excess over one actor's competence, context, tools and access; declared questions about a governed outcome; potentially overlapping frames and actors; changes between activations; and access to owning sources and copied, projected or compressed surfaces. P0 is recovered, including actor change without private-memory transfer and an open world; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 are cited as independent; P4b is derived from P0 and P2 with non-reacquirable step-produced facts, and P5 from P0 and P6 with the open-world premise.

grounding.quote:
They are conditions of the work this family governs, not
commitments, and do not follow from finite capacity alone.

concepts.label: Foundation-to-law trace

concepts.definition: A reference frame is a finite specification of the attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations required by one evaluation family. It is an engagement unit activated and evaluated as one bounded context, distinct from selection, activation, evaluation, conjunction, translation, coverage and revision functions. Its relation is not a required schema or runtime carrier; a prompt, context packet or program projects an activated frame rather than being the frame. The referenced tuple has twelve components ⟨Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D⟩.

grounding.quote: a reference frame is a finite specification of the attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations one evaluation family requires.

concepts.label: Reference frame

concepts.definition: The declared family of questions supported by a frame, against which its sufficiency and an evaluation's inclusion are tested at the declared coordinates.

grounding.quote:
Every frame declares the evaluation family it supports. A frame with no
declared evaluation family has no testable sufficiency boundary

concepts.label: Evaluation family

concepts.definition: The selected actor's declared capability boundary, including competence, context capacity, access and tools. Fitting the envelope and adequately attending during actual use are separate questions.

grounding.quote:
Whether the actor attends adequately to a frame that fits is a separate
question, answered by actual-use evidence under
[EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#frame-qualification); a size measurement
does not answer it

concepts.label: Capability envelope

concepts.definition: Distinguishable roles for semantic law, observational evidence, evaluator application, the existing owner's operation grant where material, and disposing decision authority. Frame-set authority is human authority; actor identity is separate. Acceptance and publication authorities appear separately in the supplied declarations.
exceptions: One actor may lawfully perform several roles without collapsing them.

grounding.quote:
a frame declaration keeps these roles distinguishable even when
one actor lawfully performs several of them, and where the evaluation
performs a material operation, the existing operation owner supplies the
exact grant as a further role the declaration keeps apart

concepts.label: Authority and evaluation roles

conditions: An evaluation is performed.
concepts.definition: One closed result in the frame's declared algebra: the FOUNDATIONS §4 core or a refinement mapped into it. The named core values are satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis; the frame member applies rather than defines their meanings.
exceptions: An evaluation not performed has no evaluation result; its stop state belongs to ACTIVATION §3.

grounding.quote:
Every performed evaluation of a frame returns one closed result in the
frame's declared result algebra: the core algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), or a refinement mapped
into it under that section.

concepts.label: Closed frame evaluation result

concepts.definition: A domain's unit of semantic irreducibility, distinct from a bounded engagement unit. One frame may contain several semantic atoms and an atom may participate in several frames. Any adopting method's semantic-contraction law governs its own domain atom family.

grounding.quote:
Semantic irreducibility is a
separate question: one frame may contain several semantic atoms, and one
semantic atom may take part in several frames

concepts.label: Semantic atom

concepts.definition: A human-declared project selection of frames for a governed workspace and outcome. Its declaration includes known evaluations, envelopes, intentional overlaps, separately activated checks, dependencies or translations, authorities, exclusions, uncertainty and revision conditions. It need not be a partition, tree, stack or exhaustive ontology.

grounding.quote:
Human authority may declare an initial project frame set from accumulated
development practice, known failure modes, domain expertise, the governed
outcome's risk and knowledge of the available agents and other actors.

concepts.label: Project frame set

concepts.definition: Seven relations distinct from the frame: declare(human_authority, workspace, outcome, practices, capabilities) → frame_set; activate(frame, evaluation, subject, basis, actor) → activated_frame or activation_refusal; evaluate(activated_frame, admissible_evidence) → result, evidence and residuals; conjoin(decision_rule, frame_results) → decision, conflict or indeterminate; translate(source_frame, target_frame, value_or_evidence, mapping) → translated_value, declared_loss or refusal; audit_coverage(workspace, outcome, evaluation_inventory, frame_set) → coverage_ledger; revise(frame_set, new_evidence, failures, capability_change, topology_change) → proposed_frame_set_delta. The displayed signatures are supplemented by expressly stated direct out_of_frame and invalid_basis outcomes. Declaration belongs to §4, activation/evaluation to ACTIVATION §§1–2, return/reuse to ACTIVATION §7, conjunction/translation to §6, audit to §8 and revision to §10; EVALUATION §7 qualifies each.

grounding.quote:
The frame and the functions over it remain distinct. An application may
realise the following relations in any conforming form; the signatures
describe relations, not callable software interfaces

concepts.label: Frame method relations

conditions: Each evaluation is separately activated and returns its own closed result.
concepts.definition: Several frames evaluate the same subject, potentially sharing subject, manifold or evidence sources, while neither consumes nor influences the other's unclosed working result. This serves assurance independence, different evidence altitudes and distinct failure perspectives without itself establishing every assurance-independence condition.

grounding.quote:
Several frames may evaluate the same subject through separate activations
and return closed results. They may overlap in subject, manifold or
evidence sources; neither evaluation consumes or influences the other's
unclosed working result.

concepts.label: Independently activated co-evaluation

conditions: A declared decision rule consumes closed results.
concepts.definition: A relation combining several frames' closed results under FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results and its core algebra. This member defines no independent conjunction law; §5 defines its outcome refinements.

grounding.quote: A declared decision rule consumes the closed results of several frames.

concepts.label: Result conjunction

conditions: One frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside another.
concepts.definition: A declared transfer specifying source and target coordinates, preserved meaning, accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions. ACTIVATION §4 Refinement owns what preservation and loss must show and the licensing law; representation in a_c records preservation, introduced, removed and residual fields under AC-013. This section adds the frame-specific coordinates, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions.

grounding.quote:
One frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside another. The
translation declares source and target coordinates, preserved meaning,
accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions

concepts.label: Evidence or coordinate translation

conditions: The evaluation requires the composition.
concepts.definition: Several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning relation. Its owning application declares the composition, shared invariants, effect or decision order where material, closure, failure and conservation of semantic, operation and decision authority.
exceptions: A possible future interaction alone does not require a general composition law in every frame.

grounding.quote:
Several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning
relation. The owning application declares the composition, the shared
invariants, the effect or decision order where material, closure, failure,
and the conservation of semantic, operation and decision authority.

concepts.label: Material composition

conditions: A project declares only relations needed by its evaluations and coverage claims.
concepts.definition: Ten named possibilities: disjoint means no material variable, coordinate, evidence or result dependency shared for declared evaluations; overlapping shares some material variables, evidence or entities; complementary evaluations jointly inform one decision; alternative frames evaluate the same claim under declared capability or evidence conditions; refinement resolves another frame's aggregated material distinction; restriction evaluates a lawful subset of another's domain; translated moves values or evidence through a declared coordinate map; temporally successive evaluates a changed basis later; composed forms one governed evaluation or action; governing/subordinate inherits declared constraints where a real authority or decomposition relation exists. None is the universal default topology.

grounding.quote:
No relation is the default universal frame topology. A project declares
only the relations its evaluations and coverage claims need

concepts.label: Declared frame relation kinds

concepts.definition: Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T) binds workspace W, governed outcome G, exact basis B, known evaluation inventory E, declared frame set S and the claim's time or immutable checkpoint T.

grounding.quote:
Coverage is evaluated against the tuple Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T): the
workspace W, the governed outcome G, the exact basis B, the known
evaluation inventory E, the declared frame set S and the time or immutable
checkpoint T of the claim.

concepts.label: Exact coverage tuple

conditions: Sources are available and material; listed source categories apply where applicable.
concepts.definition: Known evaluations derived by the coverage evaluator from every material available source, recording provenance and materiality. Sources include goals, intent, product definition, requirements, accepted method; accepted design and its ontology, identities, lifecycles, authorities and algorithms; implementation capabilities and observable behaviour; operational, release, security, safety and governance obligations; direct/indirect dependencies and seams; evidence, tests, scenarios, qualification and acceptance claims; tickets, check-ins, commentary, post-mortems, incidents and rejected candidates; long loops, resets, repeated repairs and rival paths; actor capability limits and invisible violations; applicable external law, contracts and standards.

grounding.quote:
The coverage evaluator derives the known evaluation inventory from every
material available source, including where applicable:

concepts.label: Known evaluation inventory

conditions: A lens becomes a frame only when separately instantiated as a bounded evaluation family.
concepts.definition: Cross-cutting audit lenses, typically outcome/capability, identity/authority, lifecycle/temporal behaviour, topology/seams, transport/representation, evidence/proof, change/failure/recovery/rollback, historical regression, and actor capability/context fit.

grounding.quote:
These are lenses (FOUNDATIONS §2): they become frames only when separately
instantiated as bounded evaluation families

concepts.label: Coverage dimensions

concepts.definition: Audit record containing at least, per evaluation: exact predicate; provenance establishing materiality; exact subject and basis; capable selected frames; required competence/context envelope; semantic owner; existing operation-owner grant for construction, transformation, admission, publication or mutation where performed, otherwise none; decision owner; required observations and provenance; material frame/seam dependencies; coverage status; and uncertainty, exclusion or re-entry residual. Statuses describe the row's coverage obligation on its exact tuple, not the evaluated claim.

grounding.quote: The ledger holds at least, for each evaluation

concepts.label: Coverage ledger

concepts.definition: Diagnosis triggered by repeated inability of a competent actor to see known material violations; repairs creating or duplicating authority paths; repeated resets after apparently valid completion; long loops without stable closure; passing proof with an unbound outcome; failures visible only after broad integration; repeated context expansion without a decidable question; actors sharing a frame name but evaluating different material relations; or topology mutation leaving prior verdicts apparently current. Diagnosis itself grants no repair authority.

grounding.quote: These observations trigger frame diagnosis

concepts.label: Frame diagnosis

concepts.definition: Minimum actor packet: frame identity/revision; evaluation/result algebra; exact subject/basis; material relations/invariants; semantic, evaluation, material operation and decision authority; admissible evidence/tools; capability/context envelope; exclusions/prohibited assumptions; declared dependencies or conjunction outputs; invalidation, stop and reconfiguration conditions. It presents one activated frame or one declared active frame configuration.

grounding.quote:
An actor receives one activated frame or one declared active frame
configuration, never an implied demand to reconstruct the complete
workspace from ambient context

concepts.label: Activation packet

conditions: Every field resolves through stable identities and source references.
concepts.definition: Carrier-neutral template sufficient to bind one declared frame for one evaluation: stable activation identity; declaration identity/revision; exact evaluation/closed algebra; exact subject or candidate; workspace, authority, dependency, configuration and time basis; material relations/invariants; exact source/semantic references; exclusions/prohibited assumptions; actor/envelope; semantic/evaluation authority; material operation authority, subject and territory; decision/acceptance/publication authority; admissible evidence/acquisition route; used dependency, overlap, input, conjunction or translation relations; expected consumer/return relation; invalidation; stop, residual, re-entry and reconfiguration conditions. The template is descriptive content, not a filled activation.

grounding.quote:
The following carrier-neutral content is sufficient to bind one declared
frame for one evaluation. It may be written in Markdown, structured data, a
prompt or another consumer-selected carrier without changing the relation

concepts.label: Minimal activation binding template

concepts.definition: Three carrier-neutral document shapes described as the least content for a frame, a frame set and an evaluation result, sufficient in Markdown or another consumer-selected carrier.

grounding.quote:
The three carrier-neutral shapes below are the least content that declares
a frame, a frame set and an evaluation result. Each is sufficient as
written in Markdown or any other consumer-selected carrier

concepts.label: Minimal declaration shapes

conditions: Optional frame relations record inputs, outputs, overlaps, conjunctions or translations actually used.
concepts.definition: Frame template with stable local identity; evaluation questions, predicates and closed algebra; workspace boundary, exact identity and version/time/topology coordinates; entities, variables, relations, states and interactions; coordinate distinction/equality; governing invariants; frame-set, semantic, evaluation, material operation and decision authorities; admissible evidence/provenance/exclusions; competence, context, access, tools, evaluation/assurance independence and configuration; irrelevant material, prohibited assumptions and out-of-frame conditions; optional used relations; invalidation/recharting changes; representative qualification cases, counterexamples and residuals.

grounding.quote:
# Frame: <stable local identity>

## Evaluation Family
<questions, predicates, and closed result algebra>

concepts.label: Minimal frame declaration template

concepts.definition: Frame-set template with stable local identity; workspace, outcome, basis and time; human declaration/acceptance authority; known evaluations/provenance; selected identities/revisions/envelopes; coverage mapping to capable frames; intentional separately activated checks, assurance independence or alternative fit; only evaluation-required conjunction/translation relations; uncovered, unknown, conditional or excluded evaluations; and history, topology, capability, evidence or outcome revision triggers.

grounding.quote: # Frame Set: <stable local identity>

concepts.label: Minimal frame-set declaration template

concepts.definition: Evaluation-result template with frame identity/revision, activation identity, evaluation, subject/basis, actor/envelope, semantic/evaluation/material operation/decision authority, admissible evidence, result, inference relation, residual uncertainty, out_of_frame residual, invalidation conditions and consuming decision or conjunction.

grounding.quote:
- result:
- inference relation:
- residual uncertainty:
- out_of_frame residual (missing relation or capability, owner, reconfiguration pressure):
- invalidation conditions:
- consuming decision or conjunction:

concepts.label: Minimal evaluation result template

concepts.definition: Historical disposition table for RF rows received from rc.2 REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md; other received rows are listed in FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION or EVALUATION. It reports conservation and successor loci, records heading-only predecessors as not applicable, and excludes the explicitly non-normative product-chain drift example as tier-2 subject matter without an additional determination. It labels communication, outcome/status mappings, out_of_frame residual content and F1 tracing as new; family inclusion and default reopening as tightenings; and semantic contraction as generalised beyond the design-specific Prime law. Its recorded dispositions decide nothing and do not independently demonstrate historical fidelity.

grounding.quote:
RF rows received by this member. Rows that land in FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION
or EVALUATION are listed in those members. Anchors are into rc.2
REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md; a locus is a section of this file unless it names
another member.

concepts.label: Source disposition record

conditions: Under the selected complete STDO basis.
concepts.definition: Tier-2 member owning urn:stdo:bounded-context:release-publication and identities/transitions for qualification, publication and selection of released cuts. Its announced scope includes release identities, project-qualified refs/subtrees, historical ref conservation, candidate construction, immutable RC publication, exact-cut qualification, monotonic version-line advancement, selectors, naming, release assets and Product subject, coordinated release-matched cohorts, acceptance, external qualification dependencies and successor-baseline conservation STDO-UP-015. It consumes rather than redefines FOUNDATION lineage/release objects and results, ACTIVATION effects, IDENTITY object identity, EVALUATION claims/acceptance, calculus layer/release separation and identity records, SPEC_METHOD lineage/version boundaries, and PRODUCT_DEFINITION installed basis/adoption/toolchain-manager meanings.
exceptions: Product meaning and consumer adoption are outside its ownership.

grounding.quote: Tier 2. Owns release publication:

This member owns the release-publication bounded context
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:release-publication` under the selected complete
STDO basis.

concepts.label: Release-publication context

concepts.definition: A published immutable point-in-time RC cut, locally named v<version>-rc.<n>, whose project ownership remains distinct even when another project uses the same local name.

grounding.quote:
Equal product-local cut
names do not collapse releases owned by different projects

concepts.label: Immutable RC cut

concepts.definition: Mutable product-local v<version> selector for the latest published immutable RC cut on one project's version line, where latest is the greatest positive published RC ordinal. It is a discovery aid, not an immutable identity.

grounding.quote:
It denotes a mutable version-line selector (FOUNDATIONS §2). The selector
points to the latest published immutable RC cut on that line, where latest
means the greatest positive RC ordinal published for that project and
version line.

concepts.label: Version-line selector

grounding.quote: It enters by a reference-only import, which grants no semantic, evaluation, operation or decision authority

constraints.statement: The member stops at engagement and defines no application profile, role mapping, product-owned frame-basis binding, domain product, runtime, workflow or assurance implementation. A specialisation retains its declaring owner's meaning and authority and neither enters nor amends this member; proximity and same spelling admit no carrier. Imported concepts retain the defining member's owner and meaning through reference-only import, granting no semantic, evaluation, operation or decision authority. A locally stated refinement names its owner and maps to the core. Core claims add no independent law, violation listings apply their cited rules, and consumers decide nothing beyond the owning rule. Added choices must remain distinguished from derived consequences.
constraints.uncertainty: Referenced import law and foundation standing are not supplied in full.

conditions: A frame is to be bound or declared inputs acquired.
exceptions: When a derived surface is stale, missing or insufficient for a named question, the deciding owning sections are acquired directly on the selected basis.

grounding.quote: A frame is bound only when every material coordinate resolves to an exact source, subject, basis, authority, evidence route, actor envelope, result relation and invalidation condition
Acquisition is read-only, grants no role, operation or decision, and a missing binding is returned with its outcome before any dependent action

constraints.statement: Every material coordinate must resolve to exact source, subject, basis, authority, evidence route, actor envelope, result relation and invalidation condition; representation cannot create, widen or replace binding. Acquire declared inputs by exact identity only from the exact selected basis. Absence from view proves neither source absence nor permission to read elsewhere; candidate sources, moving selectors and other bases are no substitutes. Acquisition is read-only and grants no role, operation or decision. Return a missing binding with its outcome before dependent action. Binding a reusable declaration to an activation loads declared relations and evidence, never an undifferentiated workspace dump; the reusable declaration does not prove that activation correct.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete acquisition and missing-binding outcome rules belong to unsupplied ACTIVATION sections.

conditions: Context is constructed for an evaluation.
exceptions: The material-sufficiency rule requires no proof that undiscovered material relations do not exist.

grounding.quote: The context starts as the material closure of the intake's seed set (the subject, outcome and affected relations it names) under that relation family, and a closure that is not finite and unique on the exact basis stops the step and is not guessed

constraints.statement: Begin with material closure of the intake's seed subject, outcome and affected relations under the material relation family. If closure is not finite and unique on the exact basis, stop with closure_unresolved rather than guess. Project closure to the selected context, recording excluded, external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive seams. Adjacency or corpus availability alone justifies neither loading nor reading material.
constraints.uncertainty: AC-010 closure and AC-011 projection are referenced but not fully supplied.

conditions: The declared envelope includes a context capacity.
exceptions: Context outside the stated measurement boundary is recorded as not measured.

grounding.quote: Where the envelope declares a context capacity, the selected context's size is measured before the actor reads it, over a stated boundary, and recorded with the capacity and the comparison; context outside the boundary is recorded as not measured.

constraints.statement: Measure selected-context size before actor reading over a stated boundary and record size, declared capacity and their comparison. The envelope owns capacity and byte/token unit; the selected execution binding owns measurement boundary and time, spend and other resource limits. Measurement applies only there, shows fit only, and creates neither a budget nor a universal gate.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed measurement procedure and applicability belong to ACTIVATION §2.

conditions: A derived surface or projected frame answers a question, or a prompt is constructed.
exceptions: Historical workaround prose is included only where a current surface still requires its constraint.

grounding.quote: a derived surface or projected frame decides standalone only the questions its own source members own
a prompt is a rendered contract over typed authority, not source law

constraints.statement: A derived surface owns no determination and answers standalone only questions owned by its declared source members. A question owned elsewhere or joining several owners returns out_of_frame naming those owners, then requires those members or a surface declaring every owner. A prompt projects only current authority references, obligations, contracts, boundaries, proof expectations, fallbacks and acquisition-selected material needed by the step. Construction starts from the highest live authority surface needed and names unresolved upstream authority gaps before fallback context is read.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced design, ODD, UX and ticket specialisations are outside the supplied text.

grounding.quote:
Unknown and out-of-frame results are lawful pressure for
   reconfiguration; they are neither failed evaluations nor implied
   acceptance

constraints.statement: No finite actor is presumed to hold the whole material workspace. A useful frame is finite and sufficient relative to its declared evaluation family, whose evaluations determine attention. Human authority may select practical sets without mechanical unique partitioning. Frames may overlap, compose, refine, restrict, translate or succeed each other; hierarchy is optional and joint use does not itself require internal-coordinate composition. Coverage is workspace/outcome/inventory/basis/time relative. Breadth, usefulness, actor and technology confer no semantic, operation or decision authority. Unknown and out-of-frame results are lawful reconfiguration pressure, neither failed evaluations nor implied acceptance. Failures, resets and invisible violations remain evidence for improving declarations, activations, actor assignments or frame sets.
constraints.uncertainty: These are source-stated core claims made precise by the laws, not additional independent rules.

conditions: A frame is declared or activated.

grounding.quote:
Every frame, declared or activated, obeys the following. The objects named
are defined in FOUNDATIONS §2.

constraints.statement: The following frame laws apply to every declared or activated frame; their named objects retain their FOUNDATIONS §2 definitions.
constraints.uncertainty: FOUNDATIONS §2 is not supplied in full.

grounding.quote:
Every frame declares the evaluation family it supports. A frame with no
declared evaluation family has no testable sufficiency boundary

constraints.statement: Every frame declares its supported evaluation family. Sufficiency is testable only against that family; a module, file, service, role, persona, prompt or lens lacking a declared evaluation relation is not a frame. Family inclusion depends on whether the declared family states the decided question at the declared coordinates, never merely similar wording, name or set membership.

conditions: The frame is activated.

grounding.quote:
An activated frame contains a finite attention surface that fits the
selected actor's declared capability envelope.

constraints.statement: The activated attention surface must be finite and fit the selected actor's declared envelope. Requiring undeclared ambient memory, conversation history or effectively global workspace context makes it unreconstructable for that actor. ACTIVATION §2 owns fit measurement and applicability; EVALUATION §7 actual-use evidence answers adequate attention, which size measurement cannot establish.
constraints.uncertainty: Actual-use qualification criteria are referenced, not supplied.

conditions: A known relation's lawful change can alter the result, basis validity, evidence sufficiency, operation authority or decision authority.
exceptions: No proof of absence of undiscovered material relations is required.

grounding.quote:
Every known relation whose lawful change can alter the evaluation result,
the validity of the basis, the sufficiency of evidence, operation authority
or decision authority appears in the frame or enters through a declared
authoritative input.

constraints.statement: Every such known relation must appear in the frame or enter through declared authoritative input. Omitting any material relation makes the frame insufficient.
constraints.uncertainty: Undiscovered relations remain possible under the stated open-world premise.

conditions: A relation cannot affect the declared evaluation.
exceptions: It is needed to establish its irrelevance.

grounding.quote:
Relations that cannot affect the declared evaluation stay outside active
attention unless they are needed to establish that irrelevance.

constraints.statement: Keep irrelevant relations outside active attention. Adjacent workspace material alone does not expand the frame.

grounding.quote:
Every result binds its exact subject, basis, coordinates and evidence
scope. A stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched basis returns
`invalid_basis` or requires reactivation.

constraints.statement: Every result binds exact subject, basis, coordinates and evidence scope. Stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched basis returns invalid_basis or requires reactivation. Apparent equality of names, values, shapes, locations or topology positions never substitutes for the frame's declared coordinate equality law.

exceptions: Authority kinds may coincide in a lawful case without collapsing by default.

grounding.quote:
A frame carries and applies admitted authority. It does not mint, widen,
transfer or reconstruct semantic, evaluation, operation or decision
authority from anything that creates none.

A read-only evaluation declares no operation authority; an effectful one inherits the exact operation grant from its existing owner. A proxy for human authority keeps its identity distinct from the human authority's

constraints.statement: Frames carry only admitted authority bound to its owner and scope; they never mint, widen, transfer or reconstruct it from actor identity, capability, evidence shape, implementation reachability, frame selection, declaration, activation, execution or role naming. Read-only evaluation declares no operation authority; effectful evaluation inherits its exact existing owner's grant. Human-authority proxies retain identities distinct from human authority.
constraints.uncertainty: The full admitted-grant and bounded-proxy laws are external references.

exceptions: One actor may lawfully perform several distinguishable roles.

grounding.quote:
The separation of semantic law, evidence, the evaluator's application
and the disposing decision authority is
[EVALUATION §2](EVALUATION.md#2-separation)'s.
The evaluator applies the frame's declared invariants, evidence rules and result algebra and records every assumption whose failure could change the result

constraints.statement: A frame declaration distinguishes semantic definition, observations, evaluator application and result disposition, adding the exact existing operation-owner grant role when a material operation is performed. The evaluator applies declared invariants, evidence rules and result algebra, recording every assumption whose failure could change the result.
constraints.uncertainty: EVALUATION §2 owns the underlying separation law.

conditions: Frames share entities, variables, evidence or coordinates.

grounding.quote:
Shared
material establishes neither identical meaning nor identical basis,
authority or result. Every cross-frame equality or translation an
evaluation uses is declared where it is used

constraints.statement: Shared material establishes no identity of meaning, basis, authority or result. Declare every cross-frame equality or translation at its use.

exceptions: A consumer may align distinct relation structures where the governed subject warrants it.
Explicitly declared parent/child relations may apply.

grounding.quote:
Functional
decomposition, communication, authority precedence, frame configuration,
subject topology and evaluation dependency are distinct relation
structures

constraints.statement: Do not silently equate functional decomposition, communication, authority precedence, frame configuration, subject topology or evaluation dependency. Communication is exchange between frames or their activated actors; exchange alone grants no authority and creates neither decomposition nor evaluation dependency. Configuration assigns exchanges as well as responsibilities, so interpreting exchange as grant/dependency would alter authority or result without declaration.

conditions: The governing evaluation combines internal variables, transports evidence/values across frames, or treats their operations as one material execution relation.
exceptions: Using several frames alone requires no composition of their internal manifolds.
Independently activated evaluations may return closed results to one declared conjunction or decision rule.

grounding.quote:
Composition law is required only when the governing evaluation combines
their internal variables, transports evidence or values across them, or
treats their operations as one material execution relation.

constraints.statement: Require composition law only under the listed evaluation needs. Introduce material composition only when required by the evaluation, with its owning application's declared invariants, material effect/decision order, closure, failure and authority conservation.

conditions: A material topology mutation is detected, or the frame itself is materially revised.

grounding.quote:
An activated frame declares the topology changes capable of invalidating
its coordinates or its materiality judgment. A detected material topology
mutation causes reevaluation, frame revision or recharting before the
previous result is reused.

constraints.statement: Activated frames declare topology changes capable of invalidating coordinates or materiality judgments. Detected material mutation requires reevaluation, revision or recharting before reuse. Material frame revision invalidates every prior-revision-bound result for reuse, subject to the recorded re-check or reevaluation routes in Revision actions.

exceptions: An unperformed evaluation has no result, rather than a coerced core result.

grounding.quote:
nothing is
coerced to success; that a refinement adds no core value, keeps
indeterminate, out-of-frame and invalid-basis pressure explicit and raises
no result's standing; and that an evaluation not performed has no result

constraints.statement: Every performed evaluation returns exactly one closed result under the declared core or mapped refinement. Nothing is coerced to success; refinement adds no core value, suppresses none of indeterminate/out_of_frame/invalid_basis pressure, and raises no standing. The frame law defines none of the core values or stop states it applies.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete core semantics and stop-state algebra are not supplied.

conditions: A fresh competent actor is inside the declared envelope.

grounding.quote:
A fresh competent actor inside the declared capability envelope can
reconstruct the activated evaluation from the frame declaration, the exact
subject, the basis and the admissible inputs, without undocumented
conversational or historical context

constraints.statement: The declaration, exact subject, basis and admissible inputs must suffice for that actor to reconstruct the activated evaluation without undocumented conversational or historical context.

conditions: The material manifold exceeds the selected actor's envelope.

grounding.quote:
Choosing among them is human authority's, exercised directly or
in advance through the grant
the lawful responses are another actor, a refined frame or outer contract, sequenced activations, a lawful compression or `out_of_frame`

Human authority chooses directly or in advance by grant; ACTIVATION §2 distinguishes within-grant refinement/sequencing/compression from re-entry to the grant or envelope owner for another actor or larger envelope. grounding.quote:
Coverage and evaluation results retain known uncertainty. Unresolved
relations, uncovered evaluations, contested evidence and unknown capability
stay explicit.

constraints.statement: Retain known uncertainty explicitly, including unresolved relations, uncovered evaluations, contested evidence and unknown capability. Absence of a recorded counterexample is not evidence of universal completeness.

grounding.quote:

prompt format, repository layout, collaboration topology, worker count or

exceptions: Compression need not yield a unique smallest frame.

independently activated evaluation, different capability fit, different
evidence altitude or useful fault detection. Frames are merged only when

and proportional reasoning cost
the compressing step records the compression and its preservation argument

constraints.statement: Atomic engagement does not imply semantic irreducibility or merged meanings/owners. Domain semantic contraction belongs to an adopting method's supplied law. constraints.uncertainty: No adopting domain's semantic-contraction law is supplied.

conditions: Human authority declares a project frame set.
exceptions: Bottom-up reconstruction from the workspace is not required.

the subject relations they inspect

constraints.statement: Record governed workspace/outcome, known evaluation inventory, selected frames/envelopes, intentional overlaps/separate checks, known dependencies/translations, semantic/evaluation/material operation/decision/acceptance authorities, known exclusions/uncertainty and revision conditions. conditions: Selection is evaluated against known material E(W,G).
exceptions: Human authority may accept a non-minimal set whose additional cost buys material risk reduction or better actor fit.

grounding.quote:
for every
evaluation e in E(W, G), there is a frame F in S and an available actor a
inside F's capability envelope K_F such that F with a is capable of e

constraints.statement: Baseline coverage requires, for every known material evaluation, some selected frame and available actor inside its envelope capable of that evaluation. Selection also weighs context/competence, risk/consequence, acquisition/reasoning cost, evidence availability, useful independent overlap, translation/reconciliation cost, historical blind spots and reversibility. No optimisation algorithm is prescribed. These considerations create no universal ledger, benchmark, budget or measurement gate. Resource controls apply only through an explicitly selected frame and its owner's applicability/work scope; ACTIVATION §6 supplies that selection for a governed cost claim. The RF-002 activation-fit test is distinct from weighed context. Selection waives no applicable semantic, authority, evidence or independence constraint.

conditions: The activate predicate concerns activation for the exact evaluation, subject, basis and actor.
exceptions: Where no usable frame declares a required material relation or capability, activate returns out_of_frame directly.

grounding.quote: | `activate`: the frame is activated for this evaluation, subject, basis and actor | `activated_frame` | the frame declaration is bound to the exact evaluation, subject, basis and actor | `satisfied` |

constraints.statement: activated_frame maps to satisfied when the declaration is exactly bound. activation_refusal(capability) maps to out_of_frame when the frame declares a needed capability missing from the actor's envelope, naming capability and owner where given. activation_refusal(authority) maps to out_of_frame when required semantic/evaluation/operation/decision authority is not admitted, naming its owner. activation_refusal(basis) maps to invalid_basis for stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched subject/basis, including subject topology differing from the declared topology basis. If no frame/actor pairing can lawfully evaluate, return out_of_frame or the refusal whose cause holds, never proceed through implied context. Activation outcomes answer activation only; refusal performs no evaluation.

conditions: The conjunction assesses the composite predicate under its declared decision rule.
exceptions: Planned assessments lacking closed results and required coverage lacking a planned assessment are recorded beside the value, are not conjoin outcomes and map to no core value.

grounding.quote: the counterexample survives the join, and the disagreement stays unresolved for the decision authority

`decision(holds)` assesses the composite predicate and is not its
acceptance, which is a separate result

constraints.statement: decision(holds) maps to satisfied when the core conjunction is satisfied; it is not acceptance. decision(fails) maps to falsified when conjunction is falsified and no mandatory same-claim result is satisfied. conflict maps to falsified when mandatory same-claim results include both satisfied and falsified: the counterexample survives and disagreement remains unresolved for decision authority. indeterminate maps to indeterminate. A conjunction reporting out_of_frame or invalid_basis returns that value directly; basis mismatch is invalid_basis. Under declared veto or deferral, return the outcome whose cause holds for the reported core value, or the direct out_of_frame/invalid_basis value. Every refinement outcome carries exactly one core value with its predicate and cause-specific name when needed.
constraints.uncertainty: The owning conjunction algorithm and permissible veto/deferral rules are not supplied.

conditions: The translate predicate concerns entry into target coordinates as declared.

grounding.quote: | | `declared_loss` | the value or evidence is carried with a loss inside the declared accepted loss; the loss travels with it as a residual (P4b) | `satisfied` |

constraints.statement: translated_value maps to satisfied for transport with declared meaning. declared_loss also maps to satisfied only for loss within declared accepted loss, which travels as a residual. refusal(condition) maps to falsified when a declared refusal condition holds, including excess loss or failed identity/equality under the declared equality law. refusal(authority) maps to out_of_frame for semantic/evaluation/operation/decision authority mismatch whose relation to target authority is declared neither preserved nor a refusal condition; it names the authority owner. refusal(basis) maps to invalid_basis for stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched source basis/coordinate. Outcomes retain their distinct predicate, cause and core value; refused transfer or excess loss is not success.

Frames act together through four distinct relations, and only where the
evaluation requires one

Where the coverage tuple itself is stale, advanced,

constraints.statement: The row predicate is capable coverage on the tuple without unresolved frame/result/authority conflict, or a cited governing exclusion. covered maps to satisfied when a capable selected frame evaluates it without unresolved conflict; separately_covered maps to satisfied when separately activated selected frames each evaluate it without unresolved conflict; excluded_by_authority maps to satisfied for the cited governing exclusion. conditionally_covered maps to indeterminate, naming the unestablished condition and deciding evidence. conflicted maps to falsified, retaining unresolved conflict as counterexample for decision authority. uncovered maps to falsified when no capable selected frame evaluates it and no cited authority excludes it, with absence as counterexample. unknown maps to indeterminate when admissible evidence cannot decide coverage, including unknown capability or materiality. Each core value travels with the coverage predicate and status. None is a result of the covered evaluation. Exclusion meets the obligation without performing or covering the evaluation.
